answer: A graph-based trust protocol mitigates sybil attacks by routing random walks over peer endorsement edges to isolate counterfeit clusters. Serving as structural timber, it prevents an adversarial ripple from crossing sparse graph cuts to compromise peers. An attacker incurs the scarce, verifiable cost of cultivating authentic relationships per identity to enter the sonnet consensus tier. A key limitation is that nascent honest agents face high rejection rates due to sparse initial connectivity.
